clue.text: A little science provided by recipient of money in North America

indicators.note: in means the till sits inside the letters for North America

parts.note: a till is the cash drawer that receives payments in a shop

explanation.surface: A bit of science funding comes from someone in America who receives the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' simply joins SCI to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle of something, so a synonym for a little.

clue.text: Fancy it's mistakenly set aside for sacred use

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters of these words are set out wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone imagines, wrongly, that something has been reserved for religious purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'it's' is ignored; FANCYITS rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanctify is to consecrate, making a thing holy and reserving it for religious purposes.

clue.text: Astute in getting information on things to be paid

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece written on another sits above it, so the information comes before the debts

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A shrewd person is in the know about the bills that are due.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenious person is clever and inventive, close in sense to shrewd or astute.

clue.text: This sum is insufficient for betting system

indicators.note: falling short means the word lacks its final letter here

parts.note: the tote is the totalisator, the pool betting system at racecourses

explanation.surface: A gambler is told the amount staked is too little for the betting scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: TOTE is the British name for pool betting at racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a total, as in to tot up a column of figures, so it names a sum.

clue.text: Isolated street round capital of Germany is most extended

indicators.note: round says those letters go around the next piece

parts.note: isolated means lone, standing by itself

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter, the capital letter, of the word Germany

explanation.surface: A lonely road loops around Berlin, and it is the longest of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The G slips into LONE, after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Longest is the superlative of long, meaning stretched out furthest of all.

clue.text: A time to run machine supplying gas

parts.note: an era is a period of time
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A period in which to operate a device that supplies gas.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerator is a device that pumps air into water or soil, so it supplies a gas.

clue.text: Add moisture to part of garden not initially fresh

parts.note: a bed is a plot of soil in a garden for flowers

indicators.note: not initially means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: A gardener waters a stale corner of the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedew is to wet with drops, as dew does, so to add moisture to something.

clue.text: What will upset any absolute source of fairness?

indicators.note: upset says the letters of these words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what could overturn an absolute principle of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairness' looks like justice; here it is beauty, fair meaning good-looking. 'What will' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty salon makes clients look lovely, and fair is an old word for beautiful.

clue.text: Motorist not against getting out of the rain now?

indicators.note: not says the letter for against is left out

parts.note: a motorist is someone who drives a car
V for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A driver who is not opposed to sheltering from the downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming in from rain leaves you less wet than before, so in a comparative sense drier.

clue.text: Succeed in election, perhaps, but not last season

indicators.note: but not last says the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: a politician who succeeds at the polls may win a term of office

explanation.surface: A candidate wins at the ballot box but not in the final season.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is one of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Honoured individual spurned by King in dark period

indicators.note: spurned by says the king's letter is rejected and removed

parts.note: a knight is someone honoured with a title by the monarch
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A knight rejected by his king in a gloomy time.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness between sunset and sunrise.

clue.text: A couple of monarchs in country's story

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the word for country

parts.note: a nation is a country
R stands for Rex or Regina, a monarch, so two monarchs give two of that letter

explanation.surface: A tale of two rulers in a land's history.
explanation.walkthrough: A and the two Rs go in after the first letter of NATION; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the telling of a story or an account of events.

clue.text: Subsequently Hearts sacked nearly all of soccer team …

indicators.note: sacked says the letter is dismissed from the word

parts.note: subsequently means then, afterwards
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Afterwards the Heart of Midlothian football club fired most of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which makes 'sacked' look like news of the manager. A football side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer team fields eleven players, so one fewer is nearly the whole side.

clue.text: … ref and all players on pitch? They weren't playing after end of that

definitions.text: … ref and all players on pitch? They weren't playing after end of that

parts.words: … ref and all players on pitch? They weren't playing after end of that
parts.note: a football match has two sides of eleven plus a referee; after the final whistle none of them is playing any more

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the referee and every player, who stop at the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 11 across: two teams of eleven plus the referee make the total.
explanation.definitionFit: Twice eleven players plus one referee totals the number of people on a football pitch.

clue.text: What a nuisance: grass in it repeatedly (upset) confection

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of mild annoyance

indicators.note: upset in a down answer turns the whole bracketed group upside down, so it reads backwards
in places the grass between the two copies
repeatedly says the little word appears twice

parts.note: taken as written
turf is grass with its soil

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about grass getting into a sweet dish, which is spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: IT TURF IT, turned by 'upset', gives TIFRUTTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti-frutti is a confection or ice cream containing mixed chopped candied fruits.

clue.text: Sunshine State dismissed jeer

parts.note: Florida is nicknamed the Sunshine State; FL is its postal abbreviation
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Florida's team was bowled out and the crowd jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout once also meant to mock or scoff, an older sense of treating with contempt.

clue.text: Decays after half of this jams

indicators.note: after says the decaying comes behind the half word
half of takes the front two of the four letters in the word this

parts.note: rusts means decays, as iron corrodes

explanation.surface: Something rots after half of it gets stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To jam a thing into place is to push or shove it forcefully, a synonym of thrusting.

clue.text: Call to bring in a half-time recap?

indicators.note: to bring in says the call takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: to summon is to call someone

indicators.note: half takes the front two of the four letters in the word time

explanation.surface: A shout to gather players for a summary during the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A summation is a summing-up, the closing review of what has been said.

clue.text: Time of year Society's lost awkward reserve

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society; the 's is a link

indicators.note: awkward says the following word is rearranged clumsily

parts.note: ice means reserve, cool aloofness of manner

explanation.surface: A club has lost its uncomfortable formality at this time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: A solstice is either of two dates when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point, midsummer or midwinter.

clue.text: Following tremors, is boarding US lorry heading for Colorado

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the little word goes inside the truck

parts.note: in American English a semi is an articulated truck

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the word Colorado

explanation.surface: After earthquakes, someone climbs into an American truck bound for Colorado.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic describes earthquakes, so it relates to what follows on from tremors.

clue.text: Spots the writer's passages (one excluded)

parts.note: the writer is the setter, me; the 's (is) is a link

indicators.note: excluded says the numeral is left out

parts.note: aisles are passages between rows of seats
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The author notices extracts from his work, with one left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb; it is the disease's rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is an infectious illness marked by a red spotty rash, so is known by its spots.

clue.text: Trick about borders leaves you a shade embarrassed?

indicators.note: about says the trick goes around the borders

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
rims are edges or borders

explanation.surface: A prank involving edges makes you a little ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves you' only links; 'a shade' hints at a colour, not a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red, the colour of someone blushing with shame.

clue.text: Ordinary member at first in unresolved situation

indicators.note: at first puts the member in front of the ordinary letter

parts.note: a limb, an arm or leg, is a member of the body
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A regular club member is at first undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being stuck in an uncertain, undecided state awaiting resolution.

clue.text: America: Democrat not seeing university as good for employment

parts.note: USA, the United States of America

indicators.note: not seeing means the letter is missing from the colour

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Democratic Party in the US

explanation.surface: A Democrat in America ignores the university's usefulness for jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: In American politics Democrats are blue and Republicans red; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable can be put to use, so it is fit to be employed.

clue.text: Wild Sultana and Rani indulging in orgies

indicators.note: wild says these letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sultan's wife and a queen enjoy a debauched party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman Saturnalia was a riotous festival, so the adjective describes wild revelry.

clue.text: Endless story being broadcast? It's a gripper

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: An interminable tale on the radio that grips its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripper' suggests a gripping yarn, but it is a bird's claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the claw of a bird of prey, used for seizing and holding.

clue.text: Silly singer dropping book

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for book is let go

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice

explanation.surface: A foolish vocalist drops his book of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is a noun here, as in 'you silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, as a noun, is a foolish person, and so is a donkey-brained fool.

clue.text: Says nothing good of beauties bearing sex appeal and a bit of taste

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the belles hold the rest inside

parts.note: belles are beautiful women
it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of the word taste

explanation.surface: Someone disparages glamorous women who have allure and a touch of style.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle is to disparage or play down, saying nothing favourable about someone.

clue.text: Pancakes: traces of bitter lemon in one

indicators.note: traces of takes just the first letters of the two words

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pancakes with a hint of sharp lemon in each.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian pancakes made with buckwheat flour.

clue.text: Lack of an ending in novel possibly produces some criticism

indicators.note: lacking an ending means the word's last letter goes

parts.note: a novel is one example of a book

explanation.surface: A novel without a proper conclusion draws critics' scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo is a shout of disapproval, so it is a form of criticism.

clue.text: One, not half unnerved, reflected lack of engagement

indicators.note: reflected says the whole group is read in mirror image, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: not half keeps only the front half of the eight letters in unnerved

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly shaken looks back on their own boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' looks like British slang for 'very'; it keeps UNNE, and 'reflected' turns IUNNE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a lack of interest or involvement.

clue.text: Newspaper's sudden move about love in spa room?

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; the 's is a link

indicators.note: about means the lunge goes around the zero

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden forward thrust
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A tabloid reports a sudden romantic move at a health resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun lounge is a glazed room for sitting in sunshine, the sort a spa might have.
